items.title: Samsung’s Call Screening could soon get more accurate with cloud transcription
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Samsung is working on a new cloud transcription option for Call Screening. 
 It will send call voice data to the cloud for more accurate transcripts and could fall back to on-device AI if the cloud service is unavailable. 
 It could support English and Chinese at launch. 

Samsung’s Call Screening feature is currently available on some Galaxy devices running One UI 8.5 and later. It lets an AI assistant answer incoming calls, ask callers why they’re calling, and show their responses as text in real time. We first spotted the feature late last year, and it has since expanded to more Galaxy phones . However, Call Screening uses on-device AI to transcribe calls, which is great for privacy but not always very accurate. Fortunately, Samsung seems to be working on a new option that could improve transcription accuracy.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

We found strings in the One UI 9.5 beta that suggest Samsung is working on a new “Cloud transcription” option for Call Screening. If enabled, your phone will send voice data from your call to Samsung’s servers for improved transcription. When you enable it for the first time, it will show a description explaining its purpose and specifying that voice data will be sent to the cloud for processing.
items.t: Samsung’s Call Screening could soon get more accurate with cloud transcription

items.title: Samsung could follow Pixel’s Pro Zoom with new AI-powered Zoom enhancer

Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority

An Android Authority teardown has uncovered a Zoom enhancer feature in the Samsung Gallery app. 
 This Gallery tool seems to use cloud-based generative AI to generate details in a picture. 
 There’s no word on a launch window or a specific device that will debut this tool. 

Smartphone cameras can only take you so far when it comes to zoom, so manufacturers have long relied on software processing for improved zoom quality. However, some brands like Google, HONOR, and vivo are leaning on generative AI for long-range zoom . Now, it looks like Samsung could join the party with its own take on AI-powered zoom.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

We dug into the One UI 9.5 beta and manually enabled a so-called Zoom enhancer feature in the Samsung Gallery app, although we can’t actually use it yet. This feature appears under the ‘Editing’ section of Gallery settings, alongside Audio Eraser, Edit suggestions, and other tools. Tap the feature in settings and you’ll be taken to a dedicated page which lets you toggle it on or off (see the second image below).
items.t: Samsung could follow Pixel’s Pro Zoom with new AI-powered Zoom enhancer

items.title: How to avoid getting locked out of your Google account (and what to do if you are)
items.summary:
Gmail is synonymous with email. Almost everyone I come across has a personal Gmail account, which they mindlessly hand out to every service that asks for an email. Think of all the apps and offline services connected to the same Google account you’ve had since school. If, God forbid, you lose access to it , not just Google but all your connected accounts could be affected — not to forget the sweeping impact on your entire internet identity tied to it.

This isn’t to scare you but to serve as a warning that you need to lay some groundwork beforehand to ensure the impact is minimal. Here’s everything you should know and can do to avoid getting locked out of your main Google account.

items.title: Google Health is ending pairing support for older Fitbit scales on November 28
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google is ending pairing and re-pairing support for Fitbit Aria and Aria 2 smart scales on November 28, 2026. 
 Some owners are already unable to connect their scales, despite the official deadline still being days away. 
 Previously paired scales will continue syncing, but disconnecting them could mean losing automatic weight tracking for good. 

Smart home gadgets have a habit of outliving the software that makes them smart. A device can work perfectly well for years, only to lose some of its most useful features when its manufacturer decides it’s time to move on. That’s the frustration facing some longtime Fitbit Aria smart scales, which are approaching a deadline that could leave them stuck with little more than ordinary bathroom scales.

Starting November 28, 2026 , Google will stop supporting new pairing and re-pairing for the Fitbit Aria and Aria 2 smart scales. The change is tied to Google Health version 5.12, although the app has already moved past that release, with version 5.13 now rolling out .
items.t: Google Health is ending pairing support for older Fitbit scales on November 28

items.title: Samsung is building an iPhone 18 Pro Max-style ‘Safe Shipping’ mode into One UI 9.5
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals a new Safe Shipping feature in Samsung’s Device Care app that will discharge a Galaxy phone’s battery before it’s shipped. 
 The feature will likely drain the battery to 89% (and 4,320mV or lower) and lock the charge limit at 80%. The feature will likely be offered through Samsung’s Warranty Care app, potentially only when you book a mail-in repair. 
 Safe Shipping isn’t currently available on the Galaxy S26 Ultra, as it likely needs a battery that supports a transport mode, which hints at newer hardware like the Galaxy S27 series. Samsung hasn’t announced the feature yet. 

Samsung’s Galaxy S Ultra phones have been stuck at 5,000mAh for years, but that’s expected to change with the Galaxy S27 series . Certification listings have already pointed to bigger batteries for the Galaxy S27 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra . Bigger batteries come with a side effect few people think about: they’re harder to ship. Now, we’ve spotted a new Samsung feature in the One UI 9.5 beta that looks built for exactly that problem.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Samsung’s Safe Shipping feature will drain your battery before you ship your phone for a repair 
 We found strings for a new “Safe Shipping” feature in Samsung’s Device Care app v13.9.00.12, part of One UI 9.5 Beta 1 on our Galaxy S26 Ultra. When Safe Shipping is turned on, your phone will discharge its battery to prepare for shipping. Expectedly, Samsung will warn you that your phone may get warm in the process.
items.t: Samsung is building an iPhone 18 Pro Max-style ‘Safe Shipping’ mode into One UI 9.5

items.title: Samsung could end annual Galaxy Watch releases starting in 2027
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Samsung reportedly plans to skip new Galaxy Watch models in 2027, breaking its annual release tradition. 
 The move to a two-year launch cycle aims to reduce development and marketing costs. 
 Samsung plans to focus on software updates and new health features for existing Galaxy Watches. 

Not every smartwatch needs a new model every year. Apple demonstrated that when it waited two years between the Watch Ultra 2 and Ultra 3, releasing only a new color in between. And with yearly hardware improvements becoming increasingly modest, there’s a growing debate over whether annual upgrades are still necessary. Samsung could now take things a step further by abandoning yearly Galaxy Watch releases altogether.

According to a new report from South Korea’s ETNews , Samsung has decided to skip new Galaxy Watch releases in 2027 and move the lineup to a two-year launch cycle. If accurate, that would break a nine-year tradition of annual releases dating back to the first Galaxy Watch in 2018.
items.t: Samsung could end annual Galaxy Watch releases starting in 2027

items.title: Google explains the 6GB RAM and 10GB storage demands for its new 3D emoji
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google’s new 3D emoji don’t actually require 10GB of storage or consume 6GB of RAM. 
 The 3D font occupies less than 220MB, while the listed hardware requirements are safeguards for automatic downloads. 
 Google hasn’t clarified whether users can opt out of downloading the new emoji. 

Google’s new Noto 3D emoji were supposed to give Android a fresh look, but their surprisingly demanding hardware requirements have left some users scratching their heads. After all, why should a new set of emoji require 6GB of RAM and 10GB of free storage? While Google’s support page also confirmed that Samsung phones won’t receive the new designs , the hardware requirements sparked another debate, prompting Google to step in with an explanation.

The good news? The new emoji don’t actually consume 6GB of RAM or 10GB of storage. According to Google’s Mishaal Rahman (via Reddit ), who verified the details with the emoji design team, the entire 3D font takes up less than 220MB. That’s considerably larger than the roughly 3MB used by the older 2D emoji, but nowhere near 10GB.
items.t: Google explains the 6GB RAM and 10GB storage demands for its new 3D emoji

items.title: GrapheneOS just built its own RCS messaging app that makes Google Messages unnecessary
items.summary:
Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

GrapheneOS has built a proof-of-concept RCS messaging app with end-to-end encryption and compatibility with Google Messages and iOS. 
 The experimental app supports typing indicators, read receipts, reactions, and media and file sharing. 
 The initial implementation will still depend on sandboxed Google Play, but won’t require Google Messages. The eventual goal is a standalone implementation for supported carriers. 
 The RCS functionality will effectively be exclusive to GrapheneOS. 

GrapheneOS is making progress on one of its most anticipated messaging features, and it could eventually let users enjoy RCS without relying on Google Messages.
items.t: GrapheneOS just built its own RCS messaging app that makes Google Messages unnecessary
